address_quote: 331 Kenton Lands Rd Suite 300 Erlanger, KY 41018

facts.text: The brewery reports an on-site parking lot. Its FAQ does not identify designated spaces or a continuous parking-to-door route.
facts.quote: Do you have parking at the taproom? Yes! We have a large parking lot with plenty of parking available.

facts.text: The FAQ describes a patio for roughly 40 people, now covered by a roof that opens or closes with the weather. It does not specify the entry route or seating clearances.
facts.quote: Yes! We have a patio that can accommodate roughly 40 people. The patio is now covered with a roof that can open or close depending on the weather.

facts.text: The brewery cautions that its decorative scenery may frighten or excite some children and asks visitors not to play with it. Noise levels and quieter seating are not described.
facts.quote: Also, please be aware that our décor could be frightening to some or exciting to others. We ask that your children refrain from playing with the scenery, as it was only built to be decorative.

facts.text: Guests may bring their own food into the taproom; the FAQ also lists small snacks at the bar. Ingredient and allergy-handling arrangements are not specified.
facts.quote: In addition, we have a few small snacks available for purchase at the bar. Guests are also welcome to bring their own food to the taproom.

facts.text: Children are welcome, but the brewery asks that they be closely supervised for everyone’s safety.
facts.quote: Fabled Brew Works seeks to provide a family friendly environment where children are welcome. However, please realize that we are a brewery and children should be closely supervised for everyone's safety.

facts.text: For questions about the Suite 300 taproom and individual visit arrangements, the brewery lists 859-727-2337.
quote: 331 Kenton Lands Rd Suite 300 Erlanger, KY 41018

address_quote: 5016 Old Taylor Mill Rd Taylor Mill, KY 41015

facts.text: The Taylor Mill branch lists in-store pickup. The page does not explain where to collect an order or what carrying assistance is available.
The branch page gives daily hours of 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; these differ from the store locator. Confirm the current hours before travelling.
The store locator instead gives Taylor Mill daily hours of 7 a.m.–10 p.m. This conflicts with the branch page and is not a resolved schedule.
facts.quote: Taylor Mill 5016 Old Taylor Mill Rd Taylor Mill, KY 41015 In-Store Pickup Available Hours: Open Daily 7 am-10 pm

facts.text: The Taylor Mill store lists 859-491-9889 for questions about hours, pickup and visit arrangements.
All BCRTA and MTS vehicles have lifts for mobility devices.
quote: All BCRTA and MTS vehicles are mobility device lift-equipped

facts.text: BCARE serves a zone within 3/4 mile of fixed routes for riders certified by BCRTA; approval lasts five years. One personal care attendant rides free. Notify the agency of accompanying attendants when scheduling if possible.
quote: A paratransit zone buffer of 3/4 mile has been created along the fixed routes to determine who might be eligible for the paratransit services.
ADA approval comes with a five-year eligibility period.
ADA passengers must be certified by BCRTA in order to reserve ADA rides.

Personal care attendants (PCAs) are allowed on an ADA trip. One (1) PCA rides free, and all others must pay the same rate as the rider. Riders should notify of any PCAs that will be riding at the time of scheduling if possible.

facts.text: ADA trips must be booked the day before, but same-day trips are allowed when the schedule permits.
quote: ADA requires that reservations be made the day before a trip. BCRTA/MTS does allow same-day trips as the schedule allows.

facts.text: A free travel training program teaches riders to plan and ride fixed routes, paratransit and the BGo curb-to-curb service.
quote: Plan, navigate, and successfully ride BCRTA fixed route , paratransit , and BGo curb-to-curb options The Benefits of Travel Training Understanding transportation options Navigating the public transportation system Increasing your independence Supporting an active lifestyle It's free

facts.text: The agency’s FAQ describes fixed-route buses lowering to the curb and extending ramps for wheelchairs and other mobility devices. Individual stop-to-curb connections are not described.
quote: Fixed-route buses have the ability to lower to the curb to make boarding easier, and ramps extend to accommodate wheelchairs and other mobility devices.

facts.text: BCARE publishes mobility-device limits of under 34 by 48 inches and combined weight below 800 pounds. Confirm device fit and any needed modification with the agency before arranging travel.
quote: Mobility devices must be under 34″x 48″ and have a combined weight of less than 800 lbs

facts.text: The FAQ says stops are announced both inside and outside the vehicle. This is the agency’s published description, not an equipment-operation check.
quote: Stops are announced inside and outside of the vehicle.

facts.text: The agency’s boarding guide tells riders to ask the driver for help such as lowering the ramp or kneeling the bus. It asks riders to reach their stop five minutes before the scheduled arrival.
quote: Arrive to the bus stop five (5) minutes before scheduled arrival time. 2 Fare Out And Ready - No Need! Our fixed routes are always free! Simply hop on the bus of your choice and enjoy a free ride to your destination. 3 Ask For Help Ask driver for any assistance needing in boarding such as lowering the ramp or kneeling the bus.

facts.text: BCARE’s application process includes a form completed by the applicant and a clinical professional. Certification is required before reserving ADA rides.
quote: The approval process involves a form that must be completed by both the applicant and a clinical professional. ADA approval comes with a five-year eligibility period. Regional & Oxford Routes : $ FREE / trip Middletown Routes : $FREE / trip ADA services are for passengers with disabilities who are unable or find it challenging to ride fixed-line bus routes. ADA passengers must be certified by BCRTA in order to reserve ADA rides.

facts.text: Free destination travel training can teach an individual to make a specific journey and return, with instruction tailored to that person. Contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237 to ask for training.
quote: Destination Training Teaches an individual to travel from a specific destination and back, usually on a daily basis and greater riding instruction tailored to the needs of the individual 2 Group/Classroom Training Teaches an overview of the public transportation system, ie. reading the schedules and maps, basic navigation skills, and money handling. Bus tours and group trips are available during the training. 3 Train The Trainer Training Available to social service agencies who would like to learn about BCRTA and how to navigate the public transportation system. Interested In Travel Training? Interested in Travel Training? Please contact our Customer Service Department at 513.785.5237.
All mobility management and training services are offered free of charge.

facts.text: BCARE permits up to four normal-size shopping bags, secured in the cargo area. Drivers may help with bags but are not permitted to enter private residences.
quote: BCRTA drivers may assist passengers with bags, but they are not permitted to enter private residences. Please do not ask. Passengers are permitted to carry-on four (4) normal size shopping bags. Bags must be secured in a cargo area to allow all passengers to be seated.

facts.text: For reasonable modifications, contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237, Ohio Relay at 800-750-0750, or request@butlercountyrta.com. The agency invites requests for changes or exceptions to its rules, policies and procedures.
quote: Reasonable modifications include changes, exceptions, or adjustments to our rules, policies, practices, and procedures to provide everyone with the opportunity to use all RTA services. c. Reasonable Modification Requests can be made by contacting Customer Service at 513.785.5237, Ohio Relay at 800-750-0750, or by email at request@butlercountyrta.com

facts.text: At Chestnut Street Station, 97 W. Chestnut Street in Oxford, BCRTA lists indoor and outdoor waiting areas, covered bus transfer areas, real-time transit information and public restrooms it describes as accessible. Restroom equipment and routes between these areas are not specified.
quote: Butler County Regional Transit Authority operates a state-of-the-art multimodal transportation center at 97 W. Chestnut Street, on the former site of Talawanda High School. This central hub connects routes across Oxford, linking riders to Miami University, Hamilton and destinations throughout the region. The facility also supports transit operations with indoor vehicle storage, fueling, washing and maintenance. Officially named the Chestnut Street Multimodal Station and Shared Service Facility, it's built to keep Butler County moving. Take a Virtual Tour Facility Features Indoor and Outdoor Passenger Waiting Areas Accessible Public Restrooms Real-Time Transit Information Covered Bus Transfer Areas

facts.text: BCRTA says it does not own or control public parking at Chestnut Street Station and encourages arrival by bus. It identifies paid public and university-permit parking in Miami University’s adjacent Chestnut Fields lot; a step-free connection from the lot is not described.
quote: BCRTA does not own or control public parking facilities at the Chestnut Street Station. Visitors are encouraged to use the bus system to access the station or attend events. Public and university-permitted parking is available for a fee adjacent to the Station in Miami University's Chestnut Fields lot. For information on parking fees and payment methods, please visit ⁠ Miami University's parking information page

facts.text: BCARE says applicants waiting for processing are offered three consecutive days of rides as a one-time offer available to the public. Confirm the dates and booking arrangements; this does not establish continuing certification.
quote: During the application review process individuals will be offered 3 consecutive days of rides while they are waiting for the application to be processed. This is a one-time ride offer that is available to all of the public.

facts.text: BCARE’s rider guidelines require all mobility devices to be secured. The page does not describe who performs transfers or the securement procedure; discuss your equipment and assistance needs before travel.
quote: All mobility devices must be secured.

facts.text: BCARE’s guidelines prohibit eating and drinking onboard and invite reasonable-modification requests. Contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237 to discuss a needed exception before travel; no exception is guaranteed by the page.
quote: Eating or drinking is not permitted on board any vehicles.
Reasonable modifications include changes, exceptions, or adjustments to our rules, policies, practices, and procedures
Reasonable Modification Requests can be made by contacting Customer Service at 513.785.5237

facts.text: The FAQ reserves seats at the front of the bus for older passengers and riders with disabilities, and asks others to offer these seats when needed or requested by the driver.
facts.quote: Seats at the front of the bus are for seniors and riders with disabilities. Please keep these seats free or offer your seat to those who need it, or upon request of the operator.

facts.text: BCRTA’s FAQ says service is suspended during a Level 3 Snow Emergency, with notification to riders. Check current alerts before travelling in severe weather.
facts.quote: During a Level 3 Snow Emergency operations will be suspended with timely notification for our riders.

facts.text: The general passenger code asks riders to bring only what they can carry in one boarding and stow in their lap or under their seat. This is separate wording from BCARE’s four-bag cargo-area guidance; confirm which arrangements apply to your trip.
facts.quote: Make Space For Others : Bring only what you can carry in a single boarding and stow in your lap or under your seat.

facts.text: Community-room requests require at least 48 hours’ notice and can be made up to three months ahead, on a first-come basis. The Chestnut Station room is listed for Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; this is room availability, not the station’s general opening hours.
quote: Reservation requests must be made at least 48 hours in advance and may be scheduled up to three months ahead. Reservations are made on a first-come, first-served basis.
The Chestnut Station community room is available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM.

facts.text: A person aged 18 or older can reserve a community room without BCRTA membership. Events must be open to the public; the policy excludes admission fees, requested donations, fundraising and for-profit programs.
quote: Anyone 18 years or older may reserve the community room. No association or membership with BCRTA is required. All meetings and events held in the community room must be open to the public

The Community Room is Not Available for: Promotion or sale of commercial services Fundraising purposes Classes or programs conducted for profit Events that charge admission, attendance fees, or request donations

facts.text: CRC lists a paved walking path along the Ohio River connecting the center to St. Rose Recreation Area. Slope, distance and access from parking are not specified.
quote: a newly renovated paved walking path along the Ohio River connecting the center to St. Rose Rec Area.

facts.text: CRC describes the playground and outdoor workout equipment as accessible, and lists a NEOS electronic playground component. Individual equipment access and transfer arrangements are not specified.
quote: This center has a fully accessible playground, NEOS electronic playground component, outdoor accessible workout equipment, raised bed community sensory garden, an outdoor multiple sports court, and a newly renovated paved walking path along the Ohio River connecting the center to St. Rose Rec Area.

facts.text: The center lists a raised-bed community sensory garden. The page does not describe its noise conditions or say it is a quiet space.
quote: raised bed community sensory garden

facts.text: LeBlond houses CRC’s Division of Therapeutic Recreation. The center asks visitors to call for annual membership fees.
quote: LeBlond Center is headquarters for the Division of Therapeutic Recreation. This center has a fully accessible playground, NEOS electronic playground component, outdoor accessible workout equipment, raised bed community sensory garden, an outdoor multiple sports court, and a newly renovated paved walking path along the Ohio River connecting the center to St. Rose Rec Area. It is our constant goal to provide the best quality recreation services available. Please call the Recreation Center for Annual Membership Fees

facts.text: For visit planning at the Riverside Drive center, call 513-352-4013.
quote: Address: 2335 Riverside Dr. Cincinnati, OH 45202

facts.text: For CRC programs, request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at registration if you need additional assistance. This is the systemwide request process, rather than a guarantee of a particular LeBlond arrangement.
quote: If you feel an accommodation would be beneficial or necessary, please request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at the time of registration at the recreation center. This document is used to formally request additional assistance you may require.

facts.text: CRC’s Inclusion Team lists adaptive equipment, increased supervision, behavior supports and Boardmaker communication tools among accommodation types. Discuss the particular support needed for your program; this list does not establish which equipment is present at LeBlond.
quote: Types of Accommodations Changes in Rules and/or Policies Assistance with ADLs (activities of daily living) Architectural Changes Adaptive Equipment Increased Supervision Behavior Supports Specialized Training for Staff Boardmaker Tools for Communication

facts.text: CRC requires a valid Center Membership for Therapeutic Recreation and center programs. Its membership benefits are valid for 12 months from purchase.
quote: All individuals who register and participate in our Therapeutic Recreation and Center Programs must have a valid CRC Center Membership . Membership Benefits Entry to all CRC Recreation Centers Access to activities and programs advertised as “free with membership” Valid for 12 months from the date of purchase

facts.text: CRC notes separate charges for some programs, fitness access and pool access. Confirm the applicable charges with the center before registering.
quote: Please Note: Separate fees apply for certain programs, fitness access, and pool access.

facts.text: The center lists Monday–Friday hours of noon–8 p.m. and Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–2 p.m.; Sunday is listed as available for rentals. Sunday wording does not establish open drop-in access.
facts.quote: Monday 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM Tuesday 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM Wednesday 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM Thursday 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM Friday 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM Saturday 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM Sunday Available for rentals

facts.text: CRC includes assistance with activities of daily living among possible accommodation types. Request an assessment at registration to discuss your needs; the systemwide list does not guarantee personal-care or transfer assistance at LeBlond.
quote: Assistance with ADLs (activities of daily living)

If you feel an accommodation would be beneficial or necessary, please request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at the time of registration at the recreation center. This document is used to formally request additional assistance you may require.

facts.text: For consideration for a CRC Center Membership Scholarship, the Therapeutic Recreation page directs visitors to call 513-352-4023. It does not state approval criteria or promise an award.
facts.quote: If you would like to be considered for a Center Membership Scholarship, please contact us (513) 352-4023
